newsitem.title: UK: EURO VEG OILS STEADY ON CHINA TALK/USDA FORECAST.
newsitem.headline: EURO VEG OILS STEADY ON CHINA TALK/USDA FORECAST.

text.p: Midday European vegetable oil prices were steady on Wednesday supported by higher markets in Asia and the U.S.
Talk that China was interested in U.S. soy oil made sense to many traders.
"It would be a logical move by the Chinese because South America is almost sold out and there is not a lot of soy oil in Europe at the moment," said one trader.
However, traders said they did not think that China would buy a significant amount of soy oil.
"China will probable buy on a monthly basis, but the amount of oil will not be significant enough to effect the market," said another trader.
"Soy oil futures are looking overbought because at the moment there is not enough fact to backup the talk and we should see prices come back down," the trader added.
Traders said there was also the possibility of China buying rape oil from Europe, although at the moment there is no evidence of this.
"We will be more surprise if China does not buy rape oil from Europe," said a trader.
Forecast of good 1997/98 U.S. soy oil exports by the USDA and better palm oil prices on the back of a weaker Malaysian ringgit helped to fuel the buoyant mood of the market.

"There are one or two people about who are saying that Chicago speculators have wheeled out the China story to stop the market falling owing to the forecast of a record soybean crop, but most believe there maybe something in the talk this time," said another trader.
At midday Dutch soy oil was one to 1.50 guilders up while rape oil was 1.75 to 1.50 guilders higher.
Crude palm oil offers were $5 to $2.50 up while products were unchanged to $2.50 higher after olein traded at $524 for Sep/Dec and $520 for Oct/Dec.
Lauric oils were left out in the cold with prices unaffected by the China talk.
Coconut oil offers were unchanged to $5 down while palmkernel oil was $2.50 to $7.50 lower at midday.
